sentences: Parametric cubical type theory combines computational paths and univalence with principles expressing uniform behavior of polymorphic functions.
Those additional principles can prove statements unavailable in ordinary type theory, so unrestricted conservativity is not expected.
The source proposes that proofs may still translate back when their assumptions and conclusions contain no function types.
It identifies a gap between obtaining semantic conservativity results and constructing a corresponding translation or theorem at the level of syntax.
Resolving that gap would explain which ordinary statements retain the same proof strength after adding powerful parametric and higher-dimensional reasoning tools.
